name_en: Neginuta (Saitama) — steamed leek dressed in sweet vinegar-miso
summary_ja: 生産量全国2位を誇る埼玉のねぎ、なかでも甘みの強い深谷ねぎを蒸してすりごま入りの酢味噌で和えた祝いの料理。宴席では「もうすぐお開き」の合図として出されることも。
summary_en: Leek from Saitama, the country's second-largest producer, especially the sweet Fukaya variety, steamed and dressed in sesame vinegar-miso for celebrations. At banquets its appearance can signal the meal is winding down.
source_title: ねぎぬた｜うちの郷土料理｜農林水産省

name_ja: こんにゃくのみそおでん
name_en: Konnyaku no Miso Oden (Saitama) — skewered hand-made konjac glazed with sweet miso
summary_ja: こんにゃく芋の産地・寄居町風布地区や秩父地域で、生芋から手作りしたこんにゃくを串に刺して味噌だれで食べる冬の一品。市販の粉こんにゃくとは異なる独特の風味と食感が持ち味。
summary_en: Konjac made by hand from raw tubers in Yorii's Fu-nuno district and Chichibu, skewered and eaten hot with a miso glaze through winter. Home-made from raw tubers, it has a distinct texture unlike the store-bought powder version.
source_title: こんにゃくのみそおでん｜うちの郷土料理｜農林水産省

name_en: Sumitsukare (Saitama) — grated daikon simmered with dried soybeans and vegetables
summary_ja: 鬼おろしで粗くすった大根に、節分で余った乾燥大豆や油揚げを加えて煮込む北埼玉地域の行事食。初午の日にきんぴらとともに稲荷様へ供え、隣接する栃木や茨城にも似た料理がある。
summary_en: Coarsely grated daikon simmered with leftover Setsubun soybeans and fried tofu, a ritual dish from northern Saitama. Offered to the fox shrine alongside kinpira on the first Horse Day, with kindred versions in neighboring Tochigi and Ibaraki.
source_title: すみつかれ｜うちの郷土料理｜農林水産省

name_en: Yatsugashira no Kuki no Itameni — dried taro stem simmered with soy sauce and shiitake
summary_ja: 八ツ頭の茎を干した「芋がら」を水で戻し、しいたけや油揚げ、こんにゃくと炒め煮した一品。食料が乏しい時期のおかずや酒の肴として重宝され、女性の健康にもよいとされてきた。
summary_en: Dried taro stems, called imogara, rehydrated and stir-simmered with shiitake and fried tofu. It served as a side dish and drinking snack in lean times, and was thought to be good for women's health.
source_title: 八ツ頭の茎の炒め煮｜うちの郷土料理｜農林水産省

name_en: Dojo Ni — pond loach simmered with burdock in soy sauce and sugar
summary_ja: 荒川や利根川の恵みを受ける埼玉東部で、田んぼで捕れたどじょうをささがきごぼうと甘辛く煮付けた一品。栄養豊富で滋養強壮によいとされ、妊婦の栄養源としても重んじられてきた。
summary_en: Pond loach caught in the paddies of eastern Saitama, simmered sweet and savory with shaved burdock, from a land fed by the Arakawa and Tone rivers. Rich in nutrients, it was valued as a tonic and a food for pregnant women.
source_title: どじょう煮｜うちの郷土料理｜農林水産省

name_en: Kuwai no Fukumeni — arrowhead corms simmered golden with gardenia seed pods
summary_ja: 生産量全国2位のくわいを、くちなしの実で鮮やかな黄色に煮含めたおせちの一品。芽が大きく伸びる姿を立身出世になぞらえた縁起物で、綾瀬川流域の低湿地栽培から生まれた。
summary_en: Arrowhead corms, of which Saitama is the nation's second-largest producer, simmered golden with gardenia seed pods for New Year's. Its long sprouting shoot is read as a sign of career success, grown in the low wetlands along the Ayase river.
source_title: くわいの含め煮｜うちの郷土料理｜農林水産省
